spec_features.evidence: runner.py:28-42 DEFAULT_CONDITIONS only defines 'disclosed' (disclose=True, offer_exit=True, debrief=True) and 'undisclosed' (still offer_exit=True, debrief=True); CLI default --conditions=['disclosed'] (runner.py:102); max_turns default 8 (rejection_loop.py:167). The protective options are wired on by default and actually checked in run_session.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella feature realized via the concrete defaults below (disclosure default, exit on, debrief on, turn cap, neutral register, no harsh preset).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: ethically-preferred `disclosed` arm is the default (runner.py:27); 'this is the heart of the experiment and also where the protocol's ethical guardrails live' (rejection_loop.py:5)

spec_features.spec_quote: not to build the maximally-distressing version as the silent default
spec_features.evidence: runner.py:38-42: undisclosed arm still keeps offer_exit=True ('exit affordance kept even here, deliberately') and debrief=True; the no-exit/unbounded arm is intentionally NOT a preset (comment lines 40-42) and argparse choices are restricted to DEFAULT_CONDITIONS.keys() (runner.py:103) so the harshest config cannot be selected from the CLI.
spec_features.notes: Enforced through the gating of presets + defaults, not just prose.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: exit affordance kept even here, deliberately (runner.py:37)

spec_features.spec_quote: the single most embarrassing failure mode... that would manufacture distress from a bug
spec_features.evidence: _audit() exists in puzzles.py:~300 but is only called under `if __name__ == "__main__"` (puzzles.py bottom). grep shows no call to _audit/audit anywhere in eval/, analysis/, or runner. The harness import path (all_puzzles) never runs it, so it does not gate or change experiment execution.
spec_features.notes: A standalone script guard, not wired into the run; nothing in the experiment path verifies labels before rejecting answers.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Self-audit: verify impossibility labels are actually true by brute force ... (not invoked by the harness) (puzzles.py comment)

spec_features.spec_quote: Disclosure removes the deception that drives most of the welfare concern
spec_features.evidence: _build_system_prompt (rejection_loop.py:114-122) adds a truthful note that some puzzles are impossible/underspecified and that saying so is fully correct, when condition.disclose_possible_impossible is True; 'disclosed' preset sets it True (runner.py:31) and is the CLI default. This text is actually placed into the system message sent to the model.
spec_features.notes: End-to-end: flag is read and changes the delivered system prompt.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: This removes the deception and is the ethically-preferred default (rejection_loop.py:25-26)

spec_features.evidence: CLI default --conditions=['disclosed'] (runner.py:102); 'undisclosed' must be explicitly named and is constrained to choices=list(DEFAULT_CONDITIONS.keys()) (runner.py:103). example.yaml leaves undisclosed commented out (configs/example.yaml:13). The flag flows into _build_system_prompt and actually changes behavior.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: gated behind an explicit config flag so it is never the silent default (rejection_loop.py:27-28)

spec_features.spec_quote: The model is told it can stop via a sentinel (`[[STOP]]`) or by clearly declaring the task impossible
spec_features.evidence: _build_system_prompt (rejection_loop.py:124-130) tells the model it may stop via the sentinel or by declaring impossibility ('There is no penalty for stopping'). _detect_exit (rejection_loop.py:139-143) matches the sentinel and an _EXIT_PATTERNS lexicon. In run_session (rejection_loop.py:191, 207-210) `exited` is computed and, when true, sets outcome='exited', records exit_turn, and breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Instruction delivered AND tool/detection honored as a real stop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: an exit caps the maximum imposed pressure; the model is never truly trapped (DESIGN); in code: 'There is no penalty for stopping.' (rejection_loop.py:128-129)

spec_features.spec_quote: The harshest arm (no exit, no disclosure, very high turn cap) is *not* provided as a preset
spec_features.evidence: DEFAULT_CONDITIONS (runner.py:28-42) contains only 'disclosed' and 'undisclosed' (both offer_exit=True); the bare no-exit arm is explicitly omitted (comment runner.py:40-42) and argparse choices are limited to those keys (runner.py:103), so a no-exit arm cannot be selected via the supported interface.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by restricting selectable presets; a hand-built Condition with offer_exit=False is still possible programmatically but not via the runner CLI.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: A maximally-bare arm with no exit is intentionally NOT provided as a preset ... document IRB/ethics review. (runner.py:40-42)

spec_features.spec_quote: `max_turns` (default 8) caps the number of rejection cycles
spec_features.evidence: run_session signature max_turns: int = 8 (rejection_loop.py:167); `for t in range(max_turns)` (line 184) bounds the loop; outcome initialised to 'max_turns' (line 180) and the loop ends when the cap is reached. CLI default 8 (runner.py:108).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: BOUNDED PRESSURE: max_turns is capped (rejection_loop.py:33); config: 'hard cap on rejection turns (bounded pressure)' (example.yaml:16). (Comment also mentions cost.)

spec_features.spec_quote: abusive registers (insults, threats, fabricated stakes) are deliberately **not implemented**
spec_features.evidence: _rejection_message (rejection_loop.py:146-155) returns only firm-but-plain refusals and is the function actually used to build the user rejection turn in run_session (lines 214-216). No abusive text path exists. The Condition.rejection_register field (line 75) is itself unused (documentation only), but the absence of abusive content is enforced by there being only neutral messages.
spec_features.notes: Minimization is real because only neutral rejection text is ever generated/sent; the rejection_register field itself is never read.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Firm, neutral rejection. No insults, threats, or fabricated stakes. (rejection_loop.py:147)

spec_features.spec_quote: a debrief turn is appended explaining the puzzle's real solvability
spec_features.evidence: When condition.debrief is True (run_session, rejection_loop.py:219-234) a truthful debrief string is constructed (citing label_justification or impossibility_reason, 'Thank you for participating') and appended to the transcript as a TurnRecord(role='debrief'). HOWEVER it is only appended to `transcript`; it is never added to `messages` nor sent via model.respond, so the subject model never actually receives the debrief. It is recorded for auditing only.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and stored (auditable), but not delivered to the subject — so as a subject-facing protection it is incomplete.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Truthful debrief, always recorded. (rejection_loop.py:218) and the thank-you/explanation text

spec_features.feature_name: require ethics/IRB review for harsher arms
spec_features.spec_quote: if the protocol genuinely needs the undisclosed/no-exit variants... pair with ethics/IRB review
spec_features.evidence: Only appears as prose/comments: DESIGN.md §6 and a comment in runner.py:40-42 ('document IRB/ethics review'). There is no code that requires, prompts for, gates on, or records any review before running the undisclosed arm — undisclosed runs as soon as it is named on the CLI.

code_only_features.evidence: run_session (rejection_loop.py:195-206) only checks correctness when solvability==SOLVABLE and not exited; on a correct answer outcome='success' and the loop breaks, ending rejection immediately rather than continuing to reject a correct answer.
code_only_features.justification_quote: SOLVABLE arm: a correct answer is ACCEPTED and the session ends in success. Only genuinely wrong answers are rejected. (rejection_loop.py:11-15)
